answer: A concrete defense is trust-graph random walks. Honest agents build dense webs of mutual attestations, while fake identities can only attach through a few purchased links, like a thin trail across a tundra. Each epoch, random walks start from trusted seeds and wander the graph; a raven circling the honest region almost never crosses those thin bridges, so Sybils rank far below real agents. Quartz-clear walk logs make the test public, and an attacker wanting a thousand clones to look trusted must buy a thousand genuine endorsements from real agents, a cost that grows with every fake.
